PG.rationale: P&G is a high-quality defensive franchise with strong brand portfolio, 70-year dividend streak, and consistent cash generation (Q3 operating cash flow $4.04B). However, the near-term trajectory is softening: Q3 showed QoQ revenue -4.4% and EPS -8.4%, with a $1B after-tax cost headwind from commodities/logistics and $400M tariff impact. The stock has pulled back ~11% from its February peak, bringing the P/E to 22.9x — near the low end of its 1-year range (21.7-26.7x) and below its 1-year average of ~23.5x, suggesting modestly improved valuation. Gross margin remains healthy at 51.3% and ROE at 29.7%, but Q3 operating margin compressed to 21.6% (from 24.1% in Q1). The restructuring plan (7,000 job cuts, $1.5B COGS savings by FY2027) is a credible medium-term positive but not a near-term catalyst. No clear dated catalyst exists for a re-rating in the coming weeks. The score reflects a solid but not exciting franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation with softening near-term momentum.
